results.summary_before: This project implements rough 24-bit VGA DACs with a digital control block for testing various patterns. It includes current-steering DACs for red and green channels and a segmented current-switching DAC for blue, with analog outputs on ua pins. It requires a 25 MHz clock, a VGA monitor, and external op-amp circuits to convert the analog outputs to the 0-0.7V range required by VGA. Silicon tests confirm the digital output works and the analog outputs show good rise/fall times, but external buffering is needed for direct VGA connection.

results.summary_before: Minilogix is a configurable 8-bit input, 8-bit output logic block with optional internal feedback, intended to function like an FPGA logic element. It is loaded serially via dedicated pins and can be used for various logic functions once configuration software is available. Testing involves loading the logic block and applying digital inputs to verify the output. It requires only a way to set digital inputs and observe outputs.

results.summary_before: This design is a read-only memory that stores ASCII encodings of LaTeX code for a few dozen Laplace transforms, generated by a Python script from the LaTeX source. The user selects a transform index on the lower six input pins, toggles reset, then asserts the character output enable to clock out the transform characters one at a time. The left-hand side output shows the transformed function F(s) and the right-hand side output shows the original function f(t), padded with spaces when lengths differ. External switches or jumpers are needed to set the input address and enable signals, and LEDs on the outputs help observe the characters; the documentation is detailed and includes verification via the same Python script.

results.summary_before: This project is functionally identical to the 8b10b decoder and multiplier design, but it is specifically intended as a test for a high-speed standard cell library. It decodes two 8b10b streams, detects the K.28.5 synchronization symbol, and can output either the decoded bytes or their product. The design can be tested by sending 8b10b encoded data and observing the outputs, with no external hardware required. The documentation is the same as the non-test version, emphasizing its use as a library characterization vehicle.
results.summary: This project is a test for a high-speed standard cell library, implementing an 8b10b decoder and multiplier. It decodes two 8b10b streams, detects the K.28.5 synchronization symbol, and can output either the decoded bytes or their product. The design can be tested by sending 8b10b encoded data and observing the outputs, with no external hardware required. While in reset, the inputs are presented on the outputs and bidirs as differential pairs.

results.summary_before: This project implements a digitally controlled oscillator that generates a frequency-adjustable clock signal from an 8-bit control input. The control input selects an oscillation period between 3 and 50 clock cycles using a priority-based scheme, with the highest active bit determining the period. A testbench is provided that simulates various input scenarios and monitors the output, with a table showing output frequencies ranging from 20 MHz down to 2.27 MHz for different input codes. The design is purely digital and requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout board itself.

results.summary_before: A fuzzy search engine that finds the best matching word in a dictionary using the bit-vector Levenshtein distance algorithm. It communicates with a host via SPI and requires an external QSPI PSRAM module to store the dictionary. Silicon testing confirmed it works but encountered a pinout mismatch with the v3 demo board, forcing a software SPI implementation limited to 500 kHz. The design is based on a 2003 paper by Heikki Hyyrö and is intended for applications needing approximate string matching.
